name: Vietnam (since 1945)
summary: Modern Vietnam: independence declared in 1945, decades of war against France and the United States, reunification in 1976, and rapid growth after the Đổi Mới reforms of 1986.

location.value: The eastern edge of mainland Southeast Asia; capital Hanoi, largest city Ho Chi Minh City.

terrain.value: Mountains cover about 40% of the land and tropical forests about 42%; the Mekong is the longest river.

climate.value: Tropical monsoon in the south and centre; monsoonal and humid subtropical in the north, with four seasons.

resources.value: Rice (the second-largest rice exporter), coffee (the second-largest coffee exporter), cashew nuts and black pepper.

disasters.value: Typhoons and tropical storms; heavy monsoon rains often cause flooding.

urbanisation.value: Hanoi is the capital and Ho Chi Minh City the largest city; traffic congestion is growing in both.

disease.value: Dengue fever; SARS (2003) was contained early; COVID-19.

migration.value: Millions fled the country after the war and during the subsidy period.

economicBase.value: Rapid industrial and export growth since the 1986 reforms; a major exporter of farm products.

tradeRoutes.value: The US buys the largest share of Vietnam’s exports, while China supplies the most imports.

wealth.value: A developing country with an upper-middle-income economy.

inequality.value: Deep poverty has fallen sharply, but the reforms widened income and gender gaps.

governmentType.value: A one-party socialist republic led by the Communist Party of Vietnam.

keyRulers.value: Ho Chi Minh led the Việt Minh, whose provisional government declared independence on 2 September 1945.

succession.value: Leaders are chosen by the Communist Party at its congresses every five years.

institutions.value: The Communist Party of Vietnam and the 500-member National Assembly.

stability.value: Stable since the end of the border war with China (1979) and the withdrawal from Cambodia (1989).

eliteConflict.value: Competition between party factions, recently through anti-corruption campaigns.

armyAndTech.value: A large army with Soviet and Russian weapons.

majorWars.value: The First Indochina War (France defeated in 1954), the Vietnam War (ended 1975), the invasion of Cambodia (1978) and a Chinese incursion (1979).

territoryChange.value: North and South were reunified in 1976; Vietnam has disputed maritime borders in the South China Sea.

alliancesRivals.value: Relied on Soviet aid; mistrust of China grew after 1979; relations with the US improved from 1995.

inventions.value: Few internationally known inventions; strong growth in software and electronics.

scienceEducation.value: The literacy rate stood at 90% in 2008.

openness.value: The Đổi Mới reforms (1986) created a socialist-oriented market economy and reintegrated Vietnam into the global economy.

communicationTransport.value: Motorcycles and scooters are the most popular road transport; the Reunification Express railway links Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City.

religion.value: Most people follow no organised religion, but many observe Vietnamese folk religion and elements of Buddhism.

languageWriting.value: Vietnamese, a tonal language of the Austroasiatic family.

artsArchitecture.value: The áo dài formal dress and a rich tradition of folk poetry (ca dao).

socialStructure.value: A fast-growing urban middle class; rural poverty in the mountains.

sharedIdentity.value: A strong identity based on resisting foreign rule (China, France, the US).

dailyLife.value: Rice, fish sauce and fresh herbs; phở noodles; a strong street food culture.

ideasReligions.value: Communism under the Communist Party; Confucianism still has some influence, and many observe folk religion and Buddhism.

riseSignals.value: The Đổi Mới reforms (1986) brought rapid industrial and export growth.

peakPeriod.value: Still exists; fast growth since the 1990s.

declineSignals.value: Not applicable: still exists. Challenges include high corruption and environmental problems.

outcome.value: Continues today as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.

overallCertainty.value: High for statistics; war tolls are estimates.
